slot.brief: Series LCR circuit with given component values and source frequency; compute the phase angle between current and voltage and state whether the circuit is inductive or capacitive.

stem: A series $LCR$ circuit has $R = 40\ \Omega$, $L = 0.10$ H and $C = 100\ \mu\text{F}$. It is connected to a source of angular frequency $500$ rad s$^{-1}$. The phase angle and nature of the circuit are:

verdicts.working: X_L=\omega L=50\,\Omega and X_C=1/(\omega C)=20\,\Omega. Hence tan(phi)=(X_L-X_C)/R=30/40=0.75, so phi≈36.9° and the circuit is inductive.

working:
$X_L = \omega L = 500(0.10) = 50\ \Omega$; $X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C} = \dfrac{1}{500(100	imes10^{-6})} = 20\ \Omega$.
$X_L > X_C$; the circuit is inductive.
$	an\phi = \dfrac{X_L-X_C}{R} = \dfrac{30}{40} = \dfrac{3}{4}$.
$\phi = 36.9^\circ$.

Independent check: X_L=\omega L=50\,\Omega and X_C=1/(\omega C)=20\,\Omega. Hence tan(phi)=(X_L-X_C)/R=30/40=0.75, so phi≈36.9° and the circuit is inductive.
